title: The grave will ask
takeaway: Don't hurt anyone, and do good. That's all that will count in the end.
scene: The heading just says 'Two couplets'. It is short, simple advice about how to live, remembering that everyone dies.

original: دشمن سجن مردے جاندے اساں وی مر جانا ایں
کسے دا دل دکھائیے نہ بدی تے ویر کمائیے نہ
transliteration: Dushman sajan marde jaande, asaan vi mar jaana ain
Kise da dil dukhaaiye na, badi te vair kamaaiye na
translation: Enemies and friends keep dying, and we will die too.
Let's not hurt anyone's heart; let's not earn evil and enmity.
couplets.story: Enemies die and friends die, and one day we'll die too. So don't hurt anybody's feelings, and don't make enemies by doing wrong.

original: کم نیکی دا کیتا احمدؔ کم حشر نوں آنا ایں
جس ویلے پے جانا قبرے فر بندے پچھتانا ایں
transliteration: Kam neki da keeta Ahmad kam hashr nu aana ain
Jis vele pai jaana qabre, phar bande pachhtaana ain
translation: Ahmad, the good you've done will help you on Judgment Day;
when you're laid in the grave, that's when a person regrets.
couplets.story: The good things you do will help you when God judges everyone. Once you're in the grave, it's too late. That's when people wish they'd done better.

deeper: A simple statement of Islamic ethics: remember death, avoid hurting others, and do good, because only good deeds will 'come to use' on the Day of Judgment. The Prophet called remembering death 'the destroyer of pleasures', a way to keep life in perspective.
why: Four lines that sum up a whole way of living.
prompt: If you knew your words would be remembered forever, what would you say differently today?
